svg.title: One end cap in section
svg.desc: A radial section through one rotor end cap, from the bore at the left to the rim at the right, with the cap plane drawn flat across the middle. The inhabited face is flat. Five curved lobes of membrane bulge out of it into the vacuum gap: lobe 1 at the rim sags 96 m, then 29, 6, 7, 13 m for lobes 2 to 5. The air-filled cap rooms lie between the face and the lobes. Tie rings sit where the lobes meet, at 850, 1,355, 1,610, 1,900 m above the ground, and a hub ring at 140 m radius; axial ties rise from them above the artificial sky, 450 m up, to the cap at the other end of the rotor. A rim compression ring of 580 square metres sits at the corner where the lobe meets the rotor wall. Below the lobes, a dashed mirror image shows the facing rotor’s cap, leaving 102.0 m clear between the deepest lobes when loaded. The axial direction is drawn four times larger than the radial.
svg.text: Hub to rim, loaded. Drawn four times deeper than wide: the sags are 6 to 96 m on spans of 255 to 850 m.
Height above the ground, metres (the ground is the rim; 2,436 m is the bore)
